lines.text: Have you ever wondered why heavy trains don't derail at high speed?
Most people assume train wheels are flat like car tires,
but flat wheels would violently shake right off the steel tracks.
In reality, train wheels are machined into tapered cones.
When a train drifts to one side, that wheel becomes wider,
automatically steering the entire train back to center.
Beneath the cabin, electric traction motors drive the axles,
gliding thousands of tons with virtually zero rolling friction.
So the wheels steer themselves, while the rails just guide the ride.
